explain.say: Imagine wearing glasses that colour how you see yourself. Some make everything look grey; others show the real you, good bits and wobbly bits. That is self-esteem: how you think and feel about yourself. Look at the two sides on the board.

faq.a: Self-esteem is how you think and feel about yourself. Healthy self-esteem means believing you matter and are okay as you are, even though you are not perfect.
Unkind comments, bullying, comparing yourself with others, especially online, and being very hard on yourself after mistakes can all pull self-esteem down.
asks: Why do I feel bad about myself?

faq.q: How can I build my self-esteem?
faq.a: Set small goals and notice when you reach them, talk kindly to yourself, do things you enjoy, and spend time with people who treat you well.
asks: How do I get more confident?

faq.q: Is high self-esteem the same as showing off?
faq.a: No. Healthy self-esteem is a quiet confidence; you do not need to prove anything. Sometimes people show off because they feel unsure inside.
asks: Is being confident the same as being big-headed?

faq.q: What if I always feel bad about myself?
faq.a: If you feel bad about yourself most of the time, talk to a trusted grown-up, a school counsellor or a doctor. You deserve support, and these feelings can get better.
asks: I hate myself, what do I do?

facts: Psychologist Morris Rosenberg created a well-known 10-question self-esteem scale in 1965, and it is still used in research today.
Research suggests self-esteem often dips in the early teenage years and then rises again through adulthood.
